Zelená zvyšuje, červená snižuje. Nejsiln: Green raises, red lowers. The strongest signal counts in full, the second by half and the third by a quarter, because signals often overlap. The usual value is the mean of your nights 8–56 days back, and ordinary variation within ±0.5 SD costs nothing. Sleep quality (efficiency over 3 nights) costs at most 20 points, and 10 without confirmation from HRV or heart rate; the watch's sleep stages don't count.
Kvalita spánku = efektivita (čas spánku: Sleep quality = efficiency (time asleep / time in bed) and the share of deep and REM sleep, against your 8-week norm. Only efficiency counts towards readiness: the mean of the last 3 nights (a single night at 0.6×), at most a quarter of a signal — and without confirmation from HRV or resting heart rate only half of that. The deep and REM share is for information only: watches agree with a sleep lab on sleep stages only about half the time, and Garmin derives them partly from HRV, which readiness already includes.
Připravenost (20–100 %) = jak daleko jso: Readiness (20–100 %) = how far your recovery markers are today from YOUR norm (the last 8 weeks): HRV below the norm and resting heart rate above it — from last night and from the 7-night mean, which is more reliable and counts a quarter more (what the watch shows as HRV status) — shorter sleep than usual (mean of 3 nights) and more time awake at night (sleep efficiency over 3 nights — at most a quarter of a signal, and without confirmation from HRV or resting heart rate only half of that). The share of deep and REM sleep is only shown: watches estimate sleep stages imprecisely and Garmin derives them partly from HRV, so it would count twice. The 7-hour threshold applies only until we know your norm; after that, habitually short sleep is a separate note. Nights under 6 hours always count, even when they are usual for you. The check-in (muscle soreness, fatigue, stress, how you slept) counts towards the Score only under Symptoms, not here. The recommendation in Training still takes it into account as before. A small deviation within your usual day-to-day variation is noise and costs nothing; the bigger the deviation, the lower the readiness. Matching signals add up: when HRV and resting heart rate are each about one of your usual variations off the norm, readiness comes out around 70 %; at almost two, around 40 %; the lowest is 20 %. Readiness reduces capacity (Load) by at most 30 %. After training on the day, readiness drops according to how demanding it was compared with your usual days (an easy session below the first threshold by at most 4 percentage points, a usual day by about 8, your hardest day in 8 weeks by 28, minutes in Z4+ add 8–12, at most 36 in total) — intensity strains recovery more than duration (Stanley et al., 2013; Seiler et al., 2007). The next day, overnight HRV, resting heart rate and sleep replace it; without overnight data, half of a hard session lingers.
